title: Simulating Fractional Stride Decrease in Binary Neural Networks Using Exponential and Logarithmic Decay: A Comparative Experiment in Energy-Efficient BNN Design
content: This paper takes a novel approach to simulating fractional stride decreases in binary neural networks (BNNs), addressing the limitations of fixed integer strides typically used in traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs). By introducing a dynamic stride adjustment mechanism that reduces stride over time using either exponential or logarithmic decay functions, the network simulates fractional strides, enabling capture of increasingly fine-grained spatial details at deeper layers. This method improves output resolution, feature extraction without increasing network complexity, and possible solutions for BNN architectures. Using synthetic data, we analyze how both decay functions impact output resolution in comparative experiments. Exponential decay produces a rapid initial stride decrease, leading to early resolution gains, while logarithmic decay offers a gradual resolution increase. Both methods are enhanced by attention mechanisms that selectively emphasize important regions in feature maps, improving spatial feature extractions. Our findings demonstrate that dynamic, asymptotic stride adjustment provides an effective method for simulating fractional strides in BNNs, with potential applications in areas such as object detection, segmentation, and autonomous systems, including spacecraft navigation and hazard detection. We also examine the trade-offs between the two decay methods in terms of resolution growth and computational overhead, contributing to ongoing research in adaptive BNN design.
